summary.intent: Get the stacked PRs (#364, #365, #367, #349) conflict-free and merged, then confirm the release shipped; when the release was found not to have happened, find out why.
summary.outcome: Resolved the #365 conflict by merging the base into it and keeping its batched version, then merged up into #367. After the user reported everything merged, found every Release run on main failing because the verify job lacked the linters needed by `just test`. Added the linter install to the verify job plus a contract-check guard, proved the guard fires, and opened a fix PR.

repo: Stacked PRs (#364 -> #365 -> #367): when the bottom branch is rebased onto main, upper branches conflict because the base commit hashes changed. Merging the new base into the upper branch (no force-push) fixes it.
Merge order for the stack is #364, then #365, then #367.
The only real conflict was `version_commit.rs`; #365's batched history version supersedes #364's parallel version.
The Release workflow's 'Verify release candidate' job runs `just test`, and it needs the linters installed. Without them, release PR creation fails and the latest release stays at 0.14.2.
There are workflow contract checks under `.github/tests/`, including `verify-release-workflow-contract.sh`, and workflows are linted.
ADR 4 makes ecosystem tools own registry reads and auth, so `cargo info` stays. A direct crates.io read would need a new ADR.
The work was done in a worktree at `.claude/worktrees/smoke-main`.

code.finding: The verify job ran tests without installing the linters. A linter install step was added right before the tests.
Added a guard that every workflow running the tests must install the linters. It was shown to fail when the install step is removed and to pass when restored.

workflow: Checking the Release workflow runs on main after a merge catches failures that PR checks missed; the release had not happened despite everything being merged.
Pair a CI fix with a contract check, and prove the check fires by temporarily removing the fix.
The guard-rail rejects shell redirection into files, so use the Read/Edit/Write tools to modify files instead.
Run verification steps as separate commands rather than chaining them.

friction: Every Release run since 22:58 the previous day failed, so releases were blocked without anyone noticing.
The guard-rail blocked appending to the contract script via shell redirection, forcing a switch to the editor tools.
The first attempt to verify the guard passing, firing and passing again in one command had to be split into separate commands.
open_items: The fix PR for the release verify job is open and still needs CI to pass and a merge.
The release itself (after 0.14.2) has not been confirmed as published once the fix lands.
The `cargo info` call, about 100 ms per crate, remains. A direct crates.io read would need a new ADR from the user.
Offline, bad-auth and half-failed-release behavior on the real tool paths was still to be tested.
